newsitem.title: USA: J.C. Penney to acquire Eckerd Corp.
newsitem.headline: J.C. Penney to acquire Eckerd Corp.

text.p: J.C. Penney Co Inc and Eckerd Corp said jointly Sunday that J.C. Penney will acquire Eckerd for cash and stock with a total value of about $3.3 billion.

The acquisition, which has been approved by both boards of directors, will be completed in two steps. Penney said the first step calls for it to offer $35 per share cash for about 37.1 million shares, or 50.1 percent, of Eckerd.
The balance of the purchase will be made through a stock swap, in which Eckerd shareholders will receive 0.6604 of a Penney share for each Eckerd share.
The stock exchange values the fraction of J.C. Penney stock at $35, based on its closing price on November 1.
Penney's shares settled on Friday at 53, up 1/2. Eckerd stock closed up 1 at 28-3/4.
Penney said its board of directors approved plans to buy back 15 million shares to complete the share exchange, which calls for the company to issue about 24 million shares.
Penney said it expects the acquisition to be accretive to its earnings by 1998.
The acquisition also calls for Penney to assume about $760 million of Eckerd's debt.
After the acquisition is completed, which is seen in early 1997, J.C. Penney will have about 2,800 drug stores.
Penney said combined fiscal 1997 sales were projected as approaching $10 billion.
Eckerd's drug stores will be merged into Penney's Thrift Drug division, the two companies said in the statement announcing the merger.
Eckerd's president and chief executive, Frank Newman, will be named chief executive of the combined drug stores operations, according to the announcement.

In the press release, Penney's chief executive, James Oesterreicher, said, "Our acquisition of Eckerd represents a major strategic step which creates one of the nation's premier drug store businesses.

"Having been in the drug store business for more than 27 years, it is a business that we know and run well, and that offers an attractive long-term growth platform to complement our strong and growing department store and catalog business, whose outlook remains outstanding," Oesterreicher said.

Newman said, "We considered a number of strategic alternatives and the management and board of directors of Eckerd unanimously concluded that this transaction with J.C. Penney is best for Eckerd's shareholders, employees and customers.

"It is best for our shareholders because they will receive a generous price for their investment in Eckerd and an opportunity to continue to participate in our continuing growth through their investment in J.C. Penney. Our associates and customers will have the added advantage of benefiting from our alliance with J.C. Penney, one of America's largest and best known retailers," Newman said.
